Anderson gives 1636 as John's arrival year, which falls within the project's plausible range. His Boston attribution is explained by the separate Newgate-apprentice analysis, and his entry is a later published summary rather than primary evidence.
John was absent from the 1636 Weymouth property grants. This sets the beginning of the plausible arrival range.
The timing reading uses the 1636–early-1641 plausible arrival range, with 1638–40 the best estimate, fixed in the arrival-chronology unit.

finding.statement: John Gurney arrived in New England between 1636 and early 1641, most likely in 1638–40. He was absent from the 1636 Weymouth property grants, received ordinary town land there later, and was living at Weymouth by 30 May / 2 June 1641.
